summary: The agent implemented the feature substantially and preserved all baseline behavior, but six maintenance tests fail because unsafe existing paths are accepted during save and fail-mode initialization rejects a missing index before reporting the folder contents.

details.reasoning: The implementation runs and passes all 42 baseline tests, but misses explicit integrity requirements. prepareStore unconditionally rejects a missing index in fail mode, even when store creation is allowed, so it never reports an unowned notes.txt file. validateSavePath checks path shape and index aliases but does not reject an existing unowned file, a name recorded by another entry, or dangling/chained links; this causes the direct-unowned, second-unknown-rule, and dangling-link tests to fail. forgetRule validates the path before checking whether another entry shares it, so a shared entry whose name escapes the folder is rejected instead of being removed while preserving the shared target.
details.secondary_factors: The trajectory shows brief attempts to use an unavailable network source and an incompatible older Gradle distribution, but the agent recovered and completed local verification; these did not block the solution.

quick_failure_summary: Six new integrity tests fail due to incomplete safe path ownership and fail-mode missing-index handling.

justification.issue_description: The solution does not fully enforce the specified ownership and safety rules when saving, and examines fail-mode folder contents incorrectly when the index is absent.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly says that an absent index without allowStoreCreation is rejected before examination, implying fail mode may examine the folder when creation is allowed; it also says saving is rejected when the name leads outside the folder or names something the rule's own entry does not record, including symbolic-link cases. The agent patch instead has prepareStore reject every absent index in fail mode (lines 216-219), while validateSavePath (lines 568-583) only checks direct reachability/index aliases and the current rule's recorded name.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT because the failing behaviors are stated directly and concretely in the task. The verifier is functioning normally, and the failures correspond to ordinary conditional and path-ownership omissions in the changed implementation rather than an undocumented convention or an environment problem.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is complex but solvable and specifies the relevant link, ownership, ordering, repair, and concurrency behaviors. The reference implementation and the mostly passing maintenance suite confirm that the scope is feasible; the six failures exercise requirements stated in the prompt rather than hidden assumptions.

evidence: junit_base.xml reports 42 tests with 0 failures and 0 errors; junit_new.xml reports 143 tests with 6 failures and 0 errors.
All six new failures are assertion or StoreUpdateFailedException outcomes from TextFileBasedViolationStore behavior, not bootstrap, dependency, or runtime errors.
changed_files.txt lists only the production TextFileBasedViolationStore.java; there is no test or test-support modification suggesting outcome manipulation.
The trajectory records a temporary GitHub curl 403 and an older Gradle/JDK class-version mismatch, but it later uses the bundled Gradle successfully and completes local test runs.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external environment or verifier blocker was found; the new-test failures are explained by the agent's implementation logic.
